items.title: Madrid–Andalucía rail repairs could take two weeks
items.body: The Transport Ministry hopes to repair the high-speed line, closed after the October 28 Urda crash that killed 69 people, in about two weeks. It gives no reopening date. A signalling failure and erroneous control-centre orders caused the crash. Operators are selling tickets only from December 13.

items.title: Court reinforces Ley de Nietos voting restrictions
items.body: The Supreme Court ordered electoral authorities to exclude 163,355 people naturalised under the Ley de Nietos from the November 29 voting rolls unless they prove descent from exiles. The precautionary suspension covers residents in Spain and abroad. It exempts 901 already certified and anyone providing a certificate before polling day.

items.title: Home completions reach highest level in 14 years
items.body: Spain completed over 60,000 homes through July, up 50% on 2025 and the highest for that period in 14 years. Supply still falls short: around 250,000 homes a year are needed to close the gap. A Bank of Spain study puts the accumulated housing deficit at 750,000 homes.

items.title: Cabinet approves contested data centre power rules
items.body: The cabinet approved a Royal Decree regulating data centres on November 20. Operators must meet power-supply conditions or accept priority disconnections. Industry group SpainDC announced a court challenge seeking suspension; the government says the rules would prevent €5 billion in extra electricity costs, a figure SpainDC disputes.

items.title: Cabinet approves carbon market expansion awaiting validation
items.body: The cabinet approved a Royal Decree-law extending the EU carbon market to road transport and buildings; parliamentary validation is still pending. Suppliers would pass carbon costs to consumers, with allowance payments planned no earlier than January 1, 2028. EU funding plus a 25% state contribution would provide €9 billion.

items.title: Bank of Spain sees contained housing risks
items.body: Bank of Spain deputy governor Soledad Núñez says housing poses no systemic financial risk, as new mortgage lending remains well below historical highs. Prices rose 12.2% in the second quarter, worsening affordability. She warns that geopolitical tensions and lower AI expectations could hit financial markets.

items.title: Spain plans Miura 5 launch within a year
items.body: Spanish Space Agency director Juan Carlos Cortés says the Miura 5 rocket is planned to launch from French Guiana within a year. It would give Spain its own means of putting payloads into orbit, joining roughly 10 countries with that capability.

items.title: Debate poll finds 7.5% reconsidering their vote
items.body: A Sigma Dos poll for El Mundo finds 7.5% of debate viewers changed their vote or now doubt their choice before the November 29 election. Some 50.5% named Partido Popular candidate Alberto Núñez Feijóo the winner, against 29% for Socialist candidate Pedro Sánchez. Housing drew the most interest.

items.title: Report finds deeper housing exclusion among non-EU residents
items.body: A forthcoming Fundación Cepaim report puts housing exclusion at 49.2% among non-EU foreigners, against 23.6% among Spaniards. Overcrowding affects 27.6% and 10.1%, respectively. Researchers point to high prices, scarce public housing, discrimination, and documentation barriers.

items.title: Election model shows tactical voting varies by province
items.body: El País has updated its model for the November 29 election using polls through November 20. It finds tactical voting could matter on the right in 34 provinces and favour the Socialists on the left in 35 of 52. It matters much less in large provinces such as Madrid and Barcelona.

items.title: Renfe urges password changes after wider data exposure
items.body: Renfe urged affected customers on November 20 to change passwords after its September cyberattack. Exposed data may include passwords, DNI or NIE (foreigner identification number) details, and travel history. Renfe first said only limited personal data was affected.

items.title: Madrid teachers march against classroom neutrality instructions
items.body: Thousands of teachers and supporters marched through Madrid on November 20, blocking Gran Vía. They opposed instructions from the Madrid regional government of Isabel Díaz Ayuso requiring classroom "neutrality" when discussing the education strike. The dispute between teachers and the regional Education Department continues.

items.title: Supreme Court upholds Balearic school language model
items.body: The Supreme Court rejected a father's request for at least 25% of classes in Spanish at a Mallorca public school, closing the judicial route. It found no proof that Spanish was marginalised. The Balearic model requires at least 50% of teaching hours in Catalan and lets schools design language plans.

items.title: Calatayud celebrates jota as Unesco recognition nears
items.body: A November 20 gala in Calatayud brought traditional Aragonese jota music together with electronics. Aragón's culture director general Pedro Olloqui said Unesco intangible heritage recognition was expected within days or, at most, weeks.

items.title: Pelayo cyberattack exposes customer and bank details
items.body: Insurer Pelayo says unauthorised access exposed customer identification, contact details, policy information, and registered IBANs. It has notified affected customers and authorities, and says its services were unaffected. Customers should watch for suspicious calls or messages and avoid sharing details with unverified contacts.
